ledger.x: c. 1450 BC (Hantili II): the Kaska first appear. 'The Kaska first appear in the Hittite prayer inscriptions', moving into the ruins of Nerik. The page's c. 1450 is the first attestation, not a founding; the land is the Pontic mountains as the page places them.

c. 1430 BC (Tudhaliya II): the Hittites fight for the Pontic frontier. 'Tudhaliya's 3rd campaign was against the Kaskas'; Arnuwanda I later prayed for the return of Nerik and named Kammama and Zalpuwa as cities now under Kaska control (both undated).

c. 1180 BC (bridged): the Hittite empire falls. The page has the Kaska possibly contributing to its fall c. 1200 and gives no treaty or last battle; the hittites dossier ends the empire c. 1180 and the contest is closed there.
Late 12th century BC: Tiglath-Pileser I defeats the Kaska, who 'disappear from all historical records'.

wars.name: Hittite campaigns against the Kaska, Tudhaliya II to Suppiluliuma I
wars.outcome: c. 1430 BC Tudhaliya II's third campaign was against the Kaskas; Arnuwanda I lost Nerik, Kammama and Zalpuwa to them (undated); Tudhaliya III and Suppiluliuma I (c. 1375-1350) set up court at Samuha and fought the Kaska and Hayasa, Piyapili leading about…

wars.name: Kaska, Hayasa-Azzi and Isuwa burn Hattusa
wars.outcome: About 1330 BC (the page's date for the letters): locusts destroyed Kaska grain and they allied with Hayasa-Azzi and Isuwa to burn Hattusa; they 'probably also burned' Sapinuwa.

wars.name: Mursili II against Pihhuniya and the Kaska revolt
wars.outcome: Around 1323 BC (Arnuwanda II) Ishupitta seceded; Mursili II later defeated the rebellion and took Pihhuniya of Tipiya, who 'ruled like a king' over the united Kaska, prisoner to Hattusa.

wars.name: Kaska sack of Hattusa under Muwatalli II
wars.outcome: Early 13th century BC: 'the Kaskas sacked Hattusa'.

certainty.note: The page calls the Kaska loosely affiliated tribes, names towns it does not locate and describes no frontier.
